clarifications.question: How are the new hooks installed, and how does hooks-uninstall remove both?
clarifications.answer: hooks-install already points core.hooksPath at scripts/hooks, so pre-push and commit-msg are two more files in that folder, made executable by hooks-install like pre-commit; each delegates to a runner mode of the same name. hooks-uninstall unsets core.hooksPath, which removes all three. The existing refusal to replace a foreign core.hooksPath or switch off the user's own hooks covers the new ones unchanged.

clarifications.question: What counts as a push to the default branch?
clarifications.answer: Any ref line git passes the pre-push hook on stdin whose remote ref is refs/heads/<default>, including a deletion. The default is the branch the remote's HEAD names (refs/remotes/<remote>/HEAD); when the remote has no HEAD ref, both master and main are treated as default.

clarifications.question: Which messages count as generated by git for merges and reverts?
clarifications.answer: A first line starting with Merge followed by branch, branches, pull request, remote-tracking branch, tag, commit or lane (the harness's own lane-land message), or starting with Revert and a double quote. They pass every commit rule.

clarifications.question: How is the message read, and what is the first line?
clarifications.answer: The file git passes as the hook's argument, with lines starting with # dropped (git's default cleanup) and leading blank lines skipped; the first remaining line is the subject. forbid patterns apply to every remaining line.

clarifications.question: Where does .harness/commit-rules.json come from, and what shape does lint accept?
clarifications.answer: templates/commit-rules.json ships to .harness/commit-rules.json through the manifest's templates list (copied when missing, like quality.json); this repository keeps its own disabled copy. Lint accepts only the keys $comment, enabled (boolean, required), subjectPattern (a valid regular expression string), maxSubjectLength (a positive integer) and forbid (an array of valid regular expression strings). A missing file means no rules.

clarifications.question: Do the hooks need npm or the full check?
clarifications.answer: No. Both run node scripts/framework-check.mjs directly and only read git and the rules file, so they take well under a second; neither runs any verification layer.
